purpose: Paromomycin is used to treat certain intestinal infections caused by parasites, such as intestinal amebiasis (an infection caused by a microscopic parasite called Entamoeba histolytica). It can also be used to help manage a condition called hepatic coma, which is when the liver is not working well and toxins build up in the blood. Your doctor prescribes it to help clear these infections or reduce harmful bacteria in your gut.
how_it_works: Paromomycin works by interfering with the ability of bacteria and parasites to make proteins they need to survive and grow. Without these proteins, the harmful organisms cannot function and they die off. Because it is mostly absorbed in the intestines and stays in the gut, it works directly where the infection is, which helps limit side effects in the rest of your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach-related and include nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, and diarrhea. You might also notice increased gas or an upset stomach. These effects are usually mild and tend to improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney problems, because paromomycin can be harmful to your kidneys if it were to get into your bloodstream in large amounts. Avoid taking it if you have ulcers or blockages in your intestines. Let your doctor know about all other medications you take, especially other antibiotics. Do not take this medication if you are allergic to aminoglycoside antibiotics. If you develop severe or bloody diarrhea, contact your doctor right away.
typical_dosing: The typical adult dose for intestinal amebiasis is 25 to 35 mg per kilogram of your body weight per day, divided into three doses taken with meals, usually for 5 to 10 days. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose that is right for you based on your weight and condition. Always take it with food to help reduce stomach upset and follow your doctor's instructions carefully.
